correctness.rationale: The 2020 published Theorem 4.5 proves exhaustiveness of flag-based minimum dominating sets; both programs independently reconstruct the 90 nine-element sets from GQ(2,2). Python exhaustively evaluates every one of 174437 subsets of at most five queries for exact Boolean traces and tests the structural criterion, while C++ independently recovers [1,30,390,2730,420,0]. A supplied depth-five tree verifies 32 distinct leaf hypotheses; each query vertex has exactly 27 positive hypotheses, excluding depth six. Shattering heredity excludes all larger supports. The checked finite universe is exhaustive, not sampled; the claim does not extrapolate beyond the doily.

value.rationale: The doily is the smallest thick generalized quadrangle with a known exact optimal-domination classification; its canonical 90 nine-sets generate a natural binary concept family on both incidence sorts. The finding supplies a complete incidence-level shattering characterization, an exact nonpure complex (1980 maximal triangles and 420 tetrahedra), and a strict VC/Littlestone separation 4 versus 5. The combinatorial content is not the already known domination number or optimizer enumeration, nor a routine normalization check: the mixed (120,180,120) facet geometry and adaptive certificate are additional invariants not given by prior domination classification.
